title: VoidSea Naval Combat Lite
description: Ships, their components, Naval Perks and component conditions from VoidSea Naval Combat Lite B0.51. Jaws is the starter vessel.

impaired.artillery: Long range is reduced to normal range, normal range to close range, and close range is lost.
impaired.control: Change of Facing score is reduced by 1.
impaired.hull: Rents open to the sea: 2d10 percent of ammunition, fuel, rations, repair parts, treasure, and fresh water are destroyed or lost; stored cargo or prisoners may be injured (GM’s discretion). Top Speed is reduced by 30 feet (minimum 0).
impaired.propulsion: Primary and Secondary Speeds are each reduced by 30 feet (minimum 0).
impaired.ram: Damage bonus during collisions is halved.

broken.artillery: Cannot be used to make attacks.
broken.control: A creature can’t take a Ship Action to Accelerate, Decelerate, or Manoeuvre the vessel.
broken.ram: Confers no damage bonus during collisions.

text.destroyed: No amount of magic or craftsmanship can restore Hit Points to it (p. 19).

repairTools.Bone: Carpenter’s or Woodcarver’s Tools (STR or DEX)
repairTools.Wood: Carpenter’s or Woodcarver’s Tools (STR or DEX)

properties.dead: Dead — Resistance to Cold and Necrotic damage.
properties.ferrous: Ferrous — magnetism-based attacks have Advantage against it; Disadvantage on saves vs magnetism-based effects.
properties.flammable: Flammable ({value}) — Resistance to Cold. Sets aflame if it takes {value}+ Fire damage in one instance; while aflame takes 2d6 Fire damage at the start of each Ship Phase (bypassing DT). Put out by a Ship Action or {value}+ Cold damage.
properties.heavy: Heavy ({value}) — reduces Top Speed by {abs} ft after all other modifiers.
properties.light: Light (+{value}) — increases Top Speed by {value} ft if at least one Propulsion component is not Broken.
properties.wind_driven: Wind-Driven — downwind +30 ft Primary; upwind or no wind: speeds 0 (optional Speed and Wind rule, p. 5).
properties.fuel: Fuel — 1 GP of fuel per hour of runtime; does not function without fuel.

shotProperties.rake: Rake — can rake a Hull within close range (p. 10)
shotProperties.advantage:hulls: Advantage vs Hulls and kaiju within close range
shotProperties.advantage:masts: Advantage vs masts and tall vertical structures within close range (GM decides)
shotProperties.anti_personnel: Anti-Personnel — ignores creatures’ size bonus to AC vs artillery
shotProperties.area: Area ({area}) — saving throw instead of attack; half damage on success
shotProperties.high_arc: High Arc — ignores cover that does not block from above
shotProperties.linking: Linking ({material}) — imposes the Linked condition on a hit

text.artilleryAction: Ship Action, Artillery Step: Artillery or Hold Artillery
text.helmStep: Accelerate / Decelerate / Zero Speed, and Manoeuvre

coreRules.title: Damage
coreRules.body: Damage that does not exceed the DT is ignored. At or below the IT a component is Impaired until fully repaired; at 0 HP it is Broken until its HP reach the IT again; reduced to 0 with 30 or more damage left over, it is destroyed.

coreRules.title: Attacks
coreRules.body: To hit is your best allowed ability modifier plus your Artillery Proficiency perks, with no Proficiency Bonus. Area shots use DC 8 plus the same. Beyond normal range attacks have Disadvantage; long range is the maximum.

coreRules.title: Raking
coreRules.body: A hit on a Hull within close range, fired perpendicular to its long axis, also damages one component and one random crew member.

categories.name: Hull
categories.description: The cladding that protects the vessel’s ribs and cargo. Destroying it is the only sure way to sink a ship.

categories.name: Control
categories.description: A cockpit of levers, switches, and wheels with which a Helmsman steers the ship.

categories.name: Propulsion
categories.description: The source of a vessel’s locomotion: sails and engines.

categories.name: Artillery
categories.description: Ship-mounted weapons that deal devastation at long range.

categories.name: Ram
categories.description: A long, heavy piece of tough material on the front of a ship, used to breach hulls in collisions.

categories.name: Miscellaneous
categories.description: The catchall for anything that doesn’t fit in the other component types.

shots.name: Beam
shots.description: A focused beam of magical energy that creates a medium-range, high damage, single-target attack.

shots.name: Burst
shots.description: A spinning plate splits the focussed beam into a dozen pulses, resulting in a slightly weaker, medium-damage attack better suited to hitting a creature.

shots.name: Refract
shots.description: An intentional misalignment of the focussing lenses diffuses the beam, allowing it to deal high damage in a wide area at very short range.

source.section: Artillery Summary; Artillery Shot Selection (p. 24); Ship Components Metadata (p. 40)

shots.name: Harpoon
shots.description: An over-sized javelin attached to a spool of rope or wire, with spring-loaded barbs. A mid-damage, low-range attack that causes a vessel or creature to become attached to the component.

shots.name: Javelin
shots.description: A huge arrow that causes high-damage to a single target at long range.

shots.name: Splinter Shot
shots.description: A dozen or more smaller arrows and lengths of metal whose weak binding tears when fired, causing the material to spread out, dealing low damage in an area at short range.

source.section: Artillery Summary; Artillery Shot Selection (p. 24); Ship Components Metadata (p. 40)

shots.name: Ball Shot
shots.description: A spherical ball, usually made of metal. A long-range, high-damage, single-target attack.

shots.name: Chain Shot
shots.description: Two smaller balls connected by a chain. When fired, the chain stretches horizontally, making it more likely to hit tall vertical structures like masts.

shots.name: Grape Shot
shots.description: A dozen or more smaller balls tightly wrapped and bound with cloth and rope. When fired, the cloth rips, causing the shot to spread out, dealing medium damage in an area at short range.

shots.name: Pebbles

traits.name: Ram
traits.text: The rammed ship is Grappled by this component (escape acceleration of 60 feet).

source.note: Damage type not stated (other Rams deal Bludgeoning).

actions.name: Whomp
actions.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +7, reach 25 ft. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) Bludgeoning damage. This attack can only target creatures or objects in contact with Jaws.

perkTrees.name: Artillerist
perkTrees.blurb: Wielding a variety of long-ranged weapons, Artillerists specialise in dealing as much damage as possible as often as possible.

perkTrees.name: Bosun
perkTrees.blurb: The repair, maintenance, improvement, and general well-being of a vessel is all down to its Bosun.

perkTrees.name: Captain
perkTrees.blurb: With wits or sheer force of personality, Captains eke the best out of their crew.

perkTrees.name: Helmsman
perkTrees.blurb: The Helmsman steers a ship through skill, instinct, and—on occasion—bravado.

perks.name: Artillery Proficiency
perks.description: You gain a +1 bonus to artillery attack rolls, as well as the save DCs of Artillery components.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, the attack and save DC bonus increases by 1.

perks.name: Crit Fisher
perks.description: Your Critical Threshold for artillery attacks is reduced by 1.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, your Critical Threshold is further reduced by 1.

perks.name: Did it Hit?
perks.range: DC by distance: 0–249 ft DC 8; 250–499 ft DC 12; 500–999 ft DC 16; 1,000–1,999 ft DC 20; 2,000–4,999 ft DC 25; 5,000–9,999 ft DC 32; 10,000+ ft DC 40 (Disadvantage in adverse conditions).
perks.description: When you make an artillery attack roll against a ship component, you can immediately take a Reaction to make a Wisdom (Perception) check. The DC is based on how far away the component is from you. If your attack roll misses and you succeed on the check, you have Advantage on the next artillery attack roll you make against that component before the end of the next Ship Phase. If your attack hits and you succeed on the check, you learn one of the following pieces of information of your choice about the component: its remaining Hit Points, its Armour Class, its Damage Threshold, or if it is Impaired.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, you learn one additional piece of information about the component on a hit.

effects.text: Reaction after shooting a component: Perception check (DC by range). Miss → Advantage on your next shot at it; hit → learn {n} of its HP, AC, DT or Impaired

perks.name: To Arms
perks.description: As a Ship Action, you can move up to your Speed and make one artillery attack roll with an Artillery component within your reach.

effects.text: Ship Action: move up to your Speed and make one artillery attack

perks.name: Anti-Personnel Specialist
perks.description: When you make an artillery attack roll against a creature, you treat that creature as if it was one size larger (maximum Gargantuan) with respect to its AC bonus against artillery attack rolls.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, you treat the target creature as one additional size larger.

perks.name: Lock In
perks.description: When you make an artillery attack roll against a ship component or structure, you gain a +3 bonus to the roll if the last artillery attack roll you made was against the same target and that attack was made since the start of your last Ship Phase.

effects.condition: same target as your last artillery attack (since your last Ship Phase)

perks.name: Ray Specialist
perks.restrictions: You must be able to cast at least one damaging cantrip.
perks.description: If you can cast at least one damaging cantrip, you can choose to expend no ammunition when you make an attack with an Energy Ray, instead charging it with your magic. If you do, the attack deals an extra 3 damage on a hit, and its damage type changes to a damage type you can deal with one of your cantrips (your choice).
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, the extra damage increases by 3.

effects.condition: when charged with your magic (no ammunition); damage type becomes one of your cantrips’

perks.name: Shot Specialist
perks.description: Artillery attacks you make with cannons and catapults deal an extra 1d6 damage of the attack’s type on a hit against ship components, structures, and kaiju.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, the extra damage increases by 1d6.

perks.name: Attunement
perks.description: You can attune to one ship component without it counting against the number of magic items to which you can normally attune.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, you can attune to one additional ship component without it counting against the number of magic items to which you can normally attune.

effects.text: Attune to {n} more ship component(s) without using your magic item attunement slots

perks.name: Credulous
perks.description: You can have Attunement to one ship component without it counting against the number of magic items to which you can normally attune.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, you can have Attunement to one additional ship component without it counting against the number of magic items to which you can normally attune.
perks.restrictions: Source text duplicates Attunement; see AMB-CREDULOUS-TEXT.

effects.text: As printed: same as Attunement, attune to {n} more ship component(s) (GM ruling pending)

perks.name: Quick Fix
perks.range: A damaged ship component within your reach
perks.resources: Ship Parts (1 per Hit Point restored)
perks.description: While you are carrying Ship Parts, you can take a Ship Action to repair a damaged ship component within your reach. Make a Strength or Wisdom check. The component regains a number of Hit Points equal to half the result of the check (rounded down), or the number of Ship Parts you are carrying, whichever is lower. Each Hit Point restored consumes 1 Ship Part.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, the number of Hit Points restored to the component increases by 2, regardless of the result of the check.

effects.text: Ship Action: repair a component in reach for ⌊STR/WIS check ÷ 2⌋{extra2} HP (1 Ship Part per HP)

perks.name: Reliable
perks.description: Using redundant mechanisms and backups, you learn how to craft extra-reliable components. You can craft and upgrade ship components to have the Reliable I quality, and you can repair components with any tier of Reliable quality.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, the level of Reliable quality increases by 1 (to Reliable II and Reliable III, respectively).

effects.text: Craft and upgrade components to Reliable {roman}; repair any Reliable component

perks.name: Robust
perks.description: Laying on extra armour plating, and then placing a bit more plating on that plating, you learn to craft components capable of withstanding a beating. You can craft and upgrade ship components to have the Robust I quality, and you can repair components with any tier of Robust quality.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, the level of Robust quality increases by 1 (to Robust II and Robust III, respectively).

effects.text: Craft and upgrade components to Robust {roman}; repair any Robust component

perks.name: Scrutinise
perks.description: You can identify the types and traits of components at a distance. As a Ship Action, you can choose one ship component on an enemy ship that you can see within 1,000 feet of you and make a Wisdom (Perception) check. The range of this action is 2,000 feet if you have a Spyglass. You learn the information that is equal to or lower than the result of your check: DC 8 name, tier, and quality; DC 12 Armour Class; DC 16 Damage Threshold; DC 20 current and maximum Hit Points; DC 24 Impairment Threshold; DC 28 if the component is magical.

effects.text: Ship Action: Perception check to learn an enemy component’s stats (1,000 ft; 2,000 with Spyglass)

perks.name: Technical
perks.restrictions: The Technical quality is not defined in the Quality tables; see AMB-TECHNICAL-QUALITY.
perks.description: With precise engineering, you learn to craft intricate and efficient components. You can craft and upgrade ship components to have the Technical I quality, and you can repair components with any tier of Technical quality.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, the level of Technical quality increases by 1 (to Technical II and Technical III, respectively).

effects.text: Craft and upgrade components to Technical {roman} (quality not defined in the beta, GM ruling pending)

perks.name: Just a Scratch
perks.range: One Impaired, non-Hull ship component within your reach
perks.duration: Until the end of the next Ship Phase
perks.description: You can temporarily restore full function to Impaired components... sometimes! As a Ship Action, you can attempt to repair one Impaired, non-Hull ship component within your reach. Roll 1d4. On a 1, the component becomes Broken until it regains Hit Points that cause its current Hit Points to exceed its Impairment Threshold. On a 2+, the component loses any penalty imposed by being Impaired until the end of the next Ship Phase.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, the size of the die you roll increases by one (from a d4 to a d6, and a d6 to a d8, respectively).

effects.text: Ship Action on an Impaired non-Hull component: roll 1{die}. 2+ ignores Impaired until end of next Ship Phase; 1 breaks it

perks.name: Low Waste Repairs
perks.description: You are adept at reusing parts and finding that thingymajig you kept in a dark cupboard because you knew it would be useful. When you repair a component, roll 1d6. On a 6, you expend half as many Ship Parts (rounded up, minimum 1 Ship Part).
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus. The result on which you expend half as many Ship Parts becomes 5–6 when you take this perk twice and 4–6 when you take this perk three times.

effects.text: When you repair, roll a d6: on {lowWaste} use only half the Ship Parts

perks.name: Weak Spot
perks.duration: Until the start of your next Ship Phase
perks.description: Once on each Ship Phase, when you hit a ship component with an artillery attack roll, you can force it to make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, if the component is not Broken, it is Impaired until the start of your next Ship Phase.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, the save DC increases by 2.

effects.text: Once per Ship Phase, on an artillery hit vs a component: DC {weakSpotDc} Con save or it is Impaired until your next Ship Phase

perks.name: Encourage
perks.duration: Until the end of the next Creature Phase
perks.description: As a Ship Action, you can encourage one ally of your choice within 120 feet of you that can hear you to act. The target gains a bonus to the next ability check it makes before the end of the next Creature Phase. The bonus equals your Charisma modifier (minimum +1).
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, you can target one additional ally when you take this action.

effects.text: Ship Action: {allies} within 120 ft get +{chaMin1} on their next ability check (until end of next Creature Phase)

perks.name: Look Alive!
perks.resources: Uses regained on a Short or Long Rest
perks.description: You can take a Reaction at the start of the Command Step to assess the Initiative scores of each vessel you can see. As a Ship Action, you can increase your vessel’s Initiative score by a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1). You can take this Ship Action once, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, the number of times you can take this action increases by one.

effects.text: Reaction: see each visible ship’s Initiative. Ship Action: +{chaMin1} to your ship’s Initiative ({uses} per rest)

perks.name: Take Aim!
perks.duration: Until the end of the next Creature Phase
perks.description: As a Ship Action while holding a Spyglass, you can relay information about the movements of a vessel you can see to an ally of your choice that can hear you. The target gains a bonus to the next attack roll it makes against any ship component on that vessel before the end of the next Creature Phase. The bonus equals your Intelligence modifier (minimum +1).
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, you can target one additional creature when you take this action.

effects.text: Ship Action with a Spyglass: {allies} get +{intMin1} on their next attack vs that ship’s components

perks.name: Boarding Party
perks.resources: Once per Short or Long Rest
perks.description: When your vessel and another vessel or kaiju come within 5 feet of each other, you can take a Reaction to order a boarding. Up to four willing creatures of your choice within 90 feet of you that can hear you can take a Reaction to move up to their Speed and make one weapon attack. As part of the Reaction to order the boarding, you can move up to your Speed and make one weapon attack. Once you take this Reaction, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

effects.text: Reaction within 5 ft of a ship: you and up to 4 allies move and attack (once per rest)

perks.name: Captain Cook
perks.duration: Ship Die lasts until a Long Rest
perks.description: While aboard a vessel, if you have ingredients and Cook’s Utensils on hand, you can prepare a hearty meal for your crew over the course of 1 hour, which can be done as part of a Short or Long Rest. The meal can be consumed by up to six creatures over the course of 10 minutes and loses its effects if it isn’t consumed within 8 hours. A creature that consumes the meal gains a Ship Die, which is a d8 that lasts until the creature finishes a Long Rest. A creature can have only one Ship Die at a time. When the creature fails a D20 Test made as part of interacting with a ship component or to avoid the effects created by a ship component, the creature can roll the Ship Die and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning the failure into a success. A Ship Die is expended when it’s rolled.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, the size of Ship Die your meal grants increases by one (from a d8 to a d10, and a d10 to a d12, respectively).

effects.text: During a rest (1 hour, Cook’s Utensils): up to 6 crew each gain a {cookDie} Ship Die to add to a failed ship roll, until their long rest

perks.name: Demoralise
perks.duration: Until the end of the next Creature Phase
perks.description: When you take the Ship Action of the Encourage perk, you can also choose one enemy within 120 feet of you to launch a volley of sneering taunts at. If the target can see or hear you, it subtracts a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) from the next ability check or attack roll it makes before the end of the next Creature Phase.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, you can target one additional enemy when you take this action.

effects.text: With Encourage: {enemies} within 120 ft take −{chaMin1} on their next check or attack

perks.name: Focus Fire
perks.description: When you take the Ship Action of the Take Aim! perk, you can specify one ship component on the target vessel. Any attack that benefits from that action and hits the specified component deals an extra 1d8 damage of the attack’s type.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, the die size of the extra damage increases by one (from a d8 to a d10, and a d10 to a d12, respectively).

effects.text: With Take Aim!: name a component; hits on it from that bonus deal +1{focusDie} damage

perks.name: Move It!
perks.duration: Until the end of the next Creature Phase
perks.description: As a Ship Action, you can command an ally that can hear you to reposition. Before the end of the next Creature Phase, the target can take a Reaction to move up to its Speed immediately after it takes a Ship Action. If a creature does not take a Ship Action, it can take a Reaction to move up to its Speed at the end of the Ship Phase.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, you can target one additional creature when you take this action.

effects.text: Ship Action: {allies} may use their Reaction to move their Speed after their Ship Action

perks.name: Take Cover!
perks.duration: Until the end of the next Creature Phase
perks.restrictions: Printed under the Naval Level 5 heading but its prerequisite says Naval Level 1; see AMB-TAKE-COVER-LEVEL.
perks.description: As a Ship Action, you can command your crew to assume defensive positions. Choose a number of allies on your vessel’s deck equal to your Intelligence or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum 1); each target that can hear you gains a +1 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws until the end of the next Creature Phase. This bonus applies only to attacks and effects that originate from outside of your vessel.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, the bonus increases by 1.

effects.text: Ship Action: {coverCount} on deck get +{n} AC and Dex saves vs attacks from outside your ship

perks.name: Full Rudder
perks.description: Once per Ship Phase, when you make one or more changes of facing, you can make a DC 13 Dexterity or Wisdom check (your choice). You have a +2 bonus to this check. On a success, you can make one additional change of facing.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, the bonus increases by 2.

effects.text: Once per Ship Phase when turning: DC 13 DEX/WIS check (+{bonus2}) for one extra change of facing

perks.name: Ramming Specialist
perks.description: When your vessel rams another, it deals an extra 1d8 Bludgeoning damage if you took a Ship Action to interact with the ship’s Control component during your vessel’s Helm Step.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, the damage increases by 1d8.

effects.text: +{n}d8 Bludgeoning when your ship rams, if you took the helm this round

perks.name: Sheet to the Wind
perks.restrictions: Not on the same turn as Give Her All She’s Got or Hard Turn.
perks.description: When you take a Ship Action to Accelerate a vessel propelled by a mast and your heading isn’t directly into the wind, you can make a DC 13 Dexterity or Wisdom check (your choice). You have a +2 bonus to this check. On a success, you increase the vessel’s Speed by 30 feet. As usual, you can’t increase the vessel’s Speed above its Top Speed. On a failure, one mast component on your vessel (randomly determined) takes 11 (2d10) Force damage, which ignores any Damage Threshold, Resistances, and Immunities. You can’t use this perk on the same turn that you use the Give Her All She’s Got or Hard Turn perk.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, the bonus increases by 2.

effects.text: When accelerating under sail (not into the wind): DC 13 DEX/WIS (+{bonus2}) for +30 ft Speed; fail = 2d10 Force to a mast

perks.name: Tracker
perks.description: When a creature makes a Tracking check while aboard your vessel, you can assist it for the duration of the check. The creature gains a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum +1).

effects.text: Creatures aboard get +{wisMin1} to Tracking checks

perks.name: Close Quarters Navigation
perks.description: You have a +2 bonus to ability checks you make to navigate your vessel through narrow spaces, like coral reefs or caves.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, the bonus increases by 2.

effects.text: +{bonus2} to checks to steer through narrow spaces like reefs and caves

perks.name: Give Her All She’s Got
perks.duration: Until the start of the next Ship Phase
perks.restrictions: Not on the same turn as Hard Turn or Sheet to the Wind.
perks.description: When you take a Ship Action to Accelerate a vessel propelled by an engine, you can push it beyond its limits, causing its Top Speed and Current Speed to increase by 30 feet until the start of the next Ship Phase. The engine component must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. The engine takes 5d10 Force damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. This damage ignores any Damage Threshold, Immunities, and Resistances. You can’t use this perk on the same turn that you use the Hard Turn or Sheet to the Wind perk.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, you can increase the vessel’s Top Speed and Current Speed by an additional 30 feet. For each additional 30 feet increase beyond the first, the DC of the saving throw increases by 2.

effects.text: When accelerating with an engine: +{speed30} ft Top and Current Speed until next Ship Phase; engine makes a DC {gearDc} Con save vs 5d10 Force

perks.name: Hard Turn
perks.restrictions: Not on the same turn as Give Her All She’s Got or Sheet to the Wind.
perks.description: When you take a Ship Action to interact with a Control component and either Accelerate, Decelerate, or Manoeuvre, you can make a DC 15 Dexterity or Wisdom check (your choice). You have a +2 bonus to this check. Success or failure, you reduce the vessel’s Current Speed by 30 feet. On a success, you can then make one additional Manoeuvre as part of that Ship Action at any point during your vessel’s Helm Step. You can’t use this perk on the same turn that you use the Give Her All She’s Got or Sheet to the Wind perk.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, the bonus increases by 2.

effects.text: With a helm action: DC 15 DEX/WIS (+{bonus2}); always −30 ft Speed, on success one extra Manoeuvre

perks.name: Jink
perks.resources: Uses regained on a Short or Long Rest
perks.description: At the start of your vessel’s Artillery Step, you take a Reaction to make a quick series of direction changes while keeping your facing. During this step, artillery attack rolls made against ship components or creatures on your vessel have Disadvantage, and artillery attack rolls made by components on your vessel have Disadvantage. You can take this Reaction once, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. For each additional time you take this perk, the number of times you can take this Reaction increases by one.

effects.text: Reaction at your Artillery Step: all artillery attacks against and from your ship have Disadvantage ({uses} per rest)

perks.name: Wind Whisperer
perks.prerequisiteText: Naval Level 5, Sheet to the Wind Perk
perks.description: A vessel that you control and that is propelled by a mast can travel an extra 12 miles per day.
perks.additional: You can take this perk a number of times equal to half of your Proficiency Bonus (rounded up). For each additional time you take this perk, the miles the vessel can travel per day increase by an additional 12.

effects.text: Your sail-powered ship travels +{miles12} miles per day

layouts.name: Jaws Deck Layout
layouts.notes: Measured from Fig. 6 (p. 43) on its 5-foot grid. Slot types and maximum sizes are exact (table, p. 15); positions and the hull outline are approximate.

source.section: Player Ship: Jaws — Deck Layout (Fig. 6); Jaws Deck Layout table (p. 15)

slots.label: Hull
slots.notes: Every ship has one Hull component (p. 14). Hulls can only be changed in a dry dock (p. 15).

slots.label: Fore emplacement (Any)
slots.notes: Artillery here has a 180° Arc of Fire (p. 43).

slots.label: Aft emplacement (Any)
slots.notes: Arc not shown in Fig. 6; general aft rule applied (AMB-M2-ARC).

templates.name: Jaws
templates.description: A mimic ship happy to accommodate your player characters. Gargantuan Vehicle (90 ft. by 30 ft.). Starter vessel from VoidSea Naval Combat Lite B0.51.

stats.source: VoidSea Naval Combat Lite B0.51, p. 44

components.overrideReason: Stat-block size exceeds the slot maximum (AMB-JAWS-SIZES).

components.label: Foresail
components.overrideReason: Stat-block size exceeds the slot maximum (AMB-JAWS-SIZES). Slot assignment per AMB-JAWS-PLACEMENT.

components.label: Mainsail Mast
components.overrideReason: Stat-block size exceeds the slot maximum (AMB-JAWS-SIZES).

rulings.title: When does a Broken component become Impaired again?
rulings.description: “Broken” (p. 19) says a component remains Broken until its current HP are equal to or higher than its IT. “Repairing Components” (p. 20) says it stays Broken until its current HP are higher than its IT, and Just a Scratch (p. 36) says “exceed its Impairment Threshold”.
rulings.affects: Component condition calculation in Combat Mode.

rulings.title: Impaired artillery shots without a close range
rulings.description: An Impaired Artillery component’s normal range is reduced to its close range and long range to its normal range (p. 19). Shots with no close range (e.g. Burst —/240/960, Harpoon —/150/—, Rock —/300/900) are left with no normal range.

options.label: As written: no normal range (every attack at Disadvantage)
GM rules per shot at the table

rulings.affects: Impaired range display for shots without a close range.

rulings.title: Magitech Cannon (Basic) Chain Shot range
rulings.description: The Artillery Shot Selection table (p. 24) gives Chain 180/360/1,440 ft for every cannon tier. The Jaws stat block (p. 44) gives Chain Shot range —/240/960 ft for its Basic cannons.
rulings.affects: Chain Shot ranges and range overlay for Magitech Cannon, Basic.

rulings.title: Saving throw ability for Area shots
rulings.description: The Area property (p. 22) calls for a saving throw but never names the ability. Only the Jaws stat block states one: Grape Shot uses Dexterity. Refract, Splinter Shot and Pebbles have no stated ability.

options.label: Leave unspecified (GM decides at the table)
Use Dexterity for all Area shots

rulings.affects: Save descriptions for Refract, Splinter Shot and Pebbles.

rulings.title: Jaws components exceed their slots’ maximum size
rulings.description: The Jaws Deck Layout table (p. 15) gives R1 max Large, P1 max Huge, M1/M2 max Large. The Jaws stat block (p. 44) lists a Huge Jaw Ram, a Gargantuan Mainsail Mast and a Gargantuan Auxiliary Mast.

options.label: Keep stat-block components as explicit GM overrides
Enforce slot sizes (GM must replace them)

rulings.affects: Compatibility warnings on the Jaws template; the template installs them as GM overrides.

rulings.title: Jaws masts differ from the general Propulsion table
rulings.description: Mainsail Mast, Superior (p. 44: HP 60, IT 24, Con +2, Gargantuan 5×5×60 ft) differs from Mainsail, Superior (p. 29: HP 65, IT 26, Con +3, Huge). Auxiliary Mast, Foresail (p. 44: AC 12, HP 50, IT 25, Con +2, no tier) matches no Auxiliary Sail tier (p. 29).

options.label: Use the general Mainsail / Auxiliary Sail entries

rulings.affects: Which masts the Jaws template installs. Both variants are in the catalogue; swap them in Design Mode.

rulings.title: Which Jaws slot holds the Foresail and the Tail Club
rulings.description: The Jaws stat block lists an Auxiliary Mast (Foresail) and a Tail Club, and the Deck Layout has two “Any” slots (M1 fore, M2 aft), but the PDF never assigns them. Slot coordinates are measured from Fig. 6 (p. 43) on a 5-foot grid and are approximate.

options.label: Foresail in M1 (fore), Tail Club in M2 (aft)
Tail Club in M1, Foresail in M2

rulings.affects: Initial placement on the Jaws template (editable in Design Mode).

rulings.title: Arc of fire of the aft “Any” emplacement (M2)
rulings.description: Fig. 6 shows arcs for the side emplacements (90°) and the front Any emplacement (180°), but not for M2. Arcs of Fire (p. 9) says aft-mounted artillery has a 180° arc backwards.
rulings.affects: Firing arc overlay for artillery installed in M2.

rulings.title: Engine Kaiju Threshold contribution
rulings.description: Noisy (X) values in the Propulsion Summary (p. 29) increase with tier (magitech 5/10/15, steam 10/20/30). The Kaiju Threshold Contributors table (p. 12) decreases with tier (magitech +15/+10/+5, steam +30/+20/+10), which matches the prose that higher-tier engines are quieter (p. 28).
rulings.affects: Kaiju Threshold shown for engines.

rulings.title: Steam Engine material
rulings.description: The Propulsion Summary (p. 29) lists Steam Engines as Magitech; the Metadata table (p. 41) and the prose (p. 28, “made almost entirely of steel, iron, and bronze”) say Metal. Material decides repair tools (p. 20).
rulings.affects: Repair tool shown for Steam Engines.

rulings.title: Ship Dexterity modifier for Initiative
rulings.description: Rolling Initiative (p. 3) adds “the ship’s Dexterity modifier”, but no ship or component in the document has a Dexterity score or modifier.

options.label: Unspecified (GM supplies a value per vehicle)

rulings.affects: Initiative formula shown in the Combat tracker.

rulings.title: How ship weight is determined
rulings.description: Component weight is “used to calculate the ship’s total weight for collisions and ramming” (p. 14), but no formula is given. Jaws states 35 tons while its mimic components have no listed weight.

options.label: Use the vessel’s stated weight when present, else the component sum

rulings.affects: Weight statistic and collision damage reference.

rulings.title: The “Technical” quality is undefined
rulings.description: The Technical perk (p. 36) and the Bosun description (p. 32) refer to a Technical quality, but the Quality tables (pp. 17–18) define Cheap, Credulous, Precise, Reliable and Robust. Technical may be Precise renamed.
rulings.affects: Technical perk description.

rulings.title: Credulous perk text duplicates Attunement
rulings.description: The Credulous perk (p. 35) repeats the Attunement perk’s effect. By analogy with Reliable, Robust and Technical it probably grants the Credulous quality, but the text does not say so.
rulings.affects: Credulous perk description.

rulings.title: Take Cover! Naval Level requirement
rulings.description: Take Cover! is printed under the Captain “Naval Level 5” heading (p. 38) but its Prerequisite line says Naval Level 1.
rulings.affects: Perk prerequisite validation.

rulings.title: “Half your Proficiency Bonus” rounding
rulings.description: Perk Anatomy (p. 31) defines “Up to Half PB” as rounded up. Attunement, Just a Scratch, Low Waste Repairs, Captain Cook, Focus Fire and Close Quarters Navigation omit “(rounded up)” in their Additional Perks text.

options.label: Round down where “(rounded up)” is missing

rulings.affects: Perk repeat-limit validation.

rulings.title: Harpoon Reel (X) value missing
rulings.description: Grappling Hooks (p. 11) says the Magitech Ballista harpoon shot has the Reel property, but the Shot Selection table (p. 24) lists no Reel property or value.

options.label: No Reel until the GM sets a value
GM supplies a Reel distance at the table

rulings.affects: Harpoon shot properties.

rulings.title: “Ship Parts” versus “Repair Parts”
rulings.description: Quick Fix and Low Waste Repairs (pp. 35–36) consume “Ship Parts”; the repair rules (p. 20) and Cargo table (p. 16) use “Repair Parts (RP)”.
rulings.affects: Repair perk descriptions.

rulings.title: Missing Jaws component data
rulings.description: The Jaws stat block gives no material, weight, CU, cost or value for its mimic components, no material or properties for the Mimicflesh Hull, no tier for the Auxiliary Mast, and no damage type for the Jaw Ram (other Rams deal Bludgeoning).

options.label: Leave blank until the GM fills them in

rulings.affects: Metadata of Jaws-specific components (editable in the Component Catalogue).

rulings.title: Ramming example uses a different Ram DT
rulings.description: The ramming example (p. 7) gives an Iron-Tipped Wooden Ram, Superior a DT of 40; the Ram table (p. 30) lists DT 49.
rulings.affects: Catalogue data (the table value is used).

rulings.title: Crafting time unit
rulings.description: The Metadata tables (pp. 40–41) list a crafting “Time” without a unit. The quality tables use hours.

options.label: Show the number without a unit

rulings.affects: Crafting time display.

rulings.title: Unresolved “page XX” references
rulings.description: The beta refers to undefined content: the Anti-Air artillery trait (p. 9), the Hold of Holding room (p. 16), enchantment options (p. 16), and “Appendix XX” reference tables. No Miscellaneous components other than the Jaws Tail Club are defined.
rulings.affects: Catalogue scope; GMs can add custom components.

rulings.title: Vessels with several Control components
rulings.description: Every ship has “at least one” Control component (p. 14). The rules do not say which Change of Facing applies when several are installed; the Helmsman uses the one they interact with (p. 5).

options.label: Use the Control the Helmsman operates

rulings.affects: Change of Facing statistic in the dashboard.

shipPhase.rule: A creature that is not Incapacitated, Stunned or Paralysed at the start of its ship’s turn takes one Ship Action in the Ship Phase. It then can’t move, take an action or Bonus Action, or use its object interaction in the Creature Phase that round (p. 4).

steps.name: Command Step
steps.text: Each creature with points in the Captain perk tree can take a Ship Action that augments the rest of the crew. A creature benefits once from a Ship Action of the same name within a round (p. 4).

steps.name: Helm Step
steps.text: A creature at a Control component within reach can take (A) Accelerate, Decelerate or Zero Speed, and (B) Manoeuvre. The ship then moves its Current Speed on its facing (p. 5).

actions.name: Accelerate
actions.text: Current Speed rises by 30 ft, never past Top Speed. Not in the same round as Decelerate.

actions.name: Decelerate
actions.text: Current Speed falls by 30 ft. Not in the same round as Accelerate.

actions.name: Zero Speed
actions.text: Furl the sails and cut the engines: every Propulsion component adds 0 ft to Top Speed, and Current Speed falls 30 ft each Helm Step.

actions.name: Manoeuvre
actions.text: Change facing as many times as the Control component’s Changes of Facing, at any point in the Helm Step.

steps.name: Artillery Step
steps.text: The ship fires as many Artillery components as it has crew taking Ship Actions; each fires once per Ship Phase (p. 4).

actions.name: Artillery
actions.text: Load, aim and fire an Artillery component within reach, choosing a shot from its Shot Selection.

actions.name: Hold Artillery
actions.text: Declare a trigger; right after it happens, take your Reaction to fire.

steps.name: Miscellaneous Step
steps.text: Take a Ship Action to cause the effect of a Miscellaneous component within reach. Bosun perks repair here (p. 4).
